title: 1st Phase of Revolutionary Activities & Home Rule Movement (1907–1919)

faqs.q: The first phase of revolutionary activities in India (1907–1917) emerged as a byproduct of which movement?
The revolutionaries of the first phase (1907–1917) drew their methodology mainly from the example of which two groups?

Consider the following statements regarding the ideology of the first-phase revolutionaries:
(I) They aimed to create a violent mass revolution throughout the country as their primary strategy
(II) They intended to strike terror in the hearts of rulers through individual heroic actions
(III) They planned to organise military conspiracies with help from Britain's enemies during the First World War
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Mass revolution and subverting Army loyalties were considered but rejected as impractical; individual heroic action and wartime military conspiracies were the actual chosen methods.

faqs.e: Prafulla Chaki shot himself dead, while Khudiram Bose was tried and hanged.

faqs.q: The Alipore conspiracy case (also called the Manicktolla bomb conspiracy) resulted in which outcome for Aurobindo Ghosh?

options.a: He was acquitted of all charges

faqs.a: He was acquitted of all charges
faqs.e: Chittaranjan Das defended Aurobindo; Barindra Ghosh and Ullaskar Dutt were given the death penalty, later commuted to life imprisonment.

faqs.q: During the Alipore conspiracy trial, the approver-turned-Crown witness who was shot dead in jail by two co-accused was:
faqs.e: He was shot by Satyendranath Bose and Kanailal Dutta.

The 1912 bomb attack on Viceroy Hardinge at Chandni Chowk, Delhi, leading to the Delhi Conspiracy trial, was staged by:
faqs.e: Viceroy Hardinge was injured but not killed; Rashbehari Bose evaded arrest by escaping in disguise.

faqs.e: This was connected to the failure of the 'German Plot'/'Zimmerman Plan' to import German arms.

faqs.q: During the First World War, the nationalist response was three-fold. Which group supported the war effort believing Britain would repay India's loyalty with self-government?
faqs.e: The Moderates supported the war as a matter of duty, while the revolutionaries sought to use the opportunity to wage war on British rule.

faqs.q: The Home Rule Movement was modelled on a similar movement in which country?
Annie Besant campaigned for self-government through her newspapers, one of which was called:
faqs.e: Her other newspaper was Commonweal.

faqs.q: Tilak set up his Indian Home Rule League in April 1916, with its headquarters at:
faqs.e: Tilak held his first Home Rule meeting at Belgaum; the league was restricted to Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar, and had six branches.

faqs.q: Annie Besant set up her All-India Home Rule League in September 1916 in which city?
faqs.e: Besant's league covered the rest of India, including Bombay city, and had 200 branches, more loosely organised than Tilak's league.

faqs.q: Who served as the organising secretary of Annie Besant's All-India Home Rule League?
Mohammad Ali Jinnah, who joined the Home Rule agitation, led which division of Besant's league?

Consider the following statements regarding groups that stayed away from the Home Rule agitation:
(I) Anglo-Indians largely did not join the agitation
(II) Most Muslims and non-Brahmins from the South did not join, fearing Home Rule would mean high-caste Hindu majority rule
(III) The Servants of India Society as a body officially opposed the Home Rule Leagues
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Some individual members of Gokhale's Servants of India Society actually joined the agitation, rather than the Society opposing it as a body.

faqs.q: In June 1917, Annie Besant and her associates B.P. Wadia and George Arundale were arrested. In protest, who renounced his knighthood?

faqs.a: Government's rejection of the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms
faqs.e: The Montagu-Chelmsford reforms, which became known in July 1918, actually further divided the nationalist ranks rather than being rejected outright.

faqs.q: The Lucknow Session of the Indian National Congress in 1916, which readmitted the Extremists, was presided over by:

Consider the following statements regarding factors that facilitated the Moderate-Extremist reunion at Lucknow (1916):
(I) Old controversies between the two groups had become largely meaningless by then
(II) The death of Gokhale and Pherozshah Mehta, leaders of Moderate opposition to the Extremists, facilitated the reunion
(III) The British government formally mediated the reconciliation
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The reunion was achieved through the efforts of Tilak and Annie Besant, not British mediation.

faqs.q: Under the Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the Muslim League, the Congress accepted the League's position on:

options.c: Reservation in the executive council only

faqs.e: This was to continue until any one community demanded joint electorates, and is regarded as a landmark in the evolution of the two-nation theory.

faqs.q: Under the Lucknow Pact's joint demands, how many years was the proposed term of the legislative council?

options.d: Chosen by the Muslim League alone

faqs.q: Montagu's August 1917 statement was made by whom, in his capacity as Secretary of State for India?

Consider the following statements on the Indian objections to Montagu's August 1917 statement:
(I) No specific time frame was given for attaining self-government
(II) The government alone was to decide the nature and timing of advance towards responsible government
(III) The statement explicitly ruled out any Indian majority in future legislatures
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The statement did not explicitly rule out future Indian representation; it left the pace and nature of progress to British discretion, which combined with the vagueness on timing formed the two main objections.
